subject: QA gating, prompt library, and customer training schedule
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jana Patel <jana@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QA gating, prompt library, and customer training schedule

Team —

As we head into the final week before the Acme pilot, I want to lock down three things that are still fuzzy and could block the go/no-go: QA gating criteria, the prompt library deliverable we promised to the customer, and the customer training schedule. I attached a draft prompt library and a provisional training workbook.

Asks: 
- Marissa — can you propose 3–4 measurable QA gates we can run on the pilot scope (e.g., pass rates on 10 canonical prompts, latency P95 under X ms for 95% of requests, no regression on hallucination checks over baseline)?
- Aditya — what remaining infra/perf gating items do you need to validate before we allow production traffic (KV cache priming strategy, warmup window, quantized model perf)? Please call out any hard blockers.
- Laura — enablement: confirm training slots and owner for the interactive demo we promised (we have 2 enterprise seats for June 12 and 19). Also recommend which playbook sections must be published before the session.

Customer context: Jana from Acme is CC'd. They want a playbook they can hand to their data science and SRE teams and two 60–90 minute training sessions. Our target is to have QA gates and docs published by EOD 6/5 so we can run a smoke validation on 6/6 and do the first training on 6/12.

I expect short replies — bullet responses are fine. If anything is blocked, flag it and suggest an alternative timeline.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt_library_v1.md (draft), training_schedule_v1.xlsx (provisional)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jana Patel <jana@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QA gating, prompt library, and customer training schedule

Thanks Marcus — quick thoughts and a proposed minimal set of QA gates below. I kept them conservative so we can get a clear pass/fail signal for the pilot.

Proposed QA gates (pilot scope: structured Q&A + short summarization):
1) Functional correctness (prompt set): >= 85% pass on 50 canonical prompts (binary pass/fail judged by rubric in prompt_library_v1.md).
2) Latency: P95 token-generation latency < 300ms on Dedicated pool under expected load profile (see notes).
3) Safety/Hallucination check: < 5% of outputs flagged by automated hallucination heuristics (and manual spot-check pass rate >= 90%).
4) Throughput stability: sustained throughput within 10% of target for 10-minute window after warmup.

Open items / clarifying questions for Aditya: 
- Do we have a reliable way to run the latency gate in CI that mirrors the Dedicated pool load? If not, propose a short runbook for how we'll emulate it.
- For the hallucination heuristic: we can run the simple regex-based filter today, but we should surface false positives to Acme in the playbook.

Training schedule: Laura, can you confirm the owners for the two sessions (intro + hands-on)? We should include an enablement checklist in the shared Drive doc (slides, demo dataset, sample prompts).

If we can close these by EOD 6/5 I’m comfortable greenlighting the smoke test on 6/6.

—Marissa
Sr. PM, Product Launches

> 1) Functional correctness ...

Quick infra/perf update and blockers: 
- Latency gate: we do not have an automated CI job that hits the Dedicated pool under identical routing today. I can spin up a short performance harness that replicates the request mix, but it will require a 3-hour reserved window on Dedicated (can we reserve tonight 11pm-2am PT?) to run at-scale. If we can't reserve Dedicated, we'll run a scaled emulation on a dev cluster which gives approximate results (±15%).
- KV cache priming: the pilot relies on prefix caching for the first-turn latency. We need to confirm the warmup script (I attached the warmup snippet to the internal repo) and schedule an initial priming pass before the smoke test. This is a hard dependency — without it first-turn P95 will be worse than target.
- Hallucination heuristics: infra can run the automated checks against the prompt set by EOD 6/5; manual spot checks will need 4–6 person-hours of review. Recommend we ask Acme to provide 10 domain-specific prompts so we can prioritize.

Blockers summary: Dedicated reservation for perf run (ask infra), finalize warmup script and run it before 6/6, confirm reviewer pool for manual checks.

ETA for infra tasks if we get the reservation and reviewers: complete by 6/5 EOD. Otherwise, push to 6/9.

-Aditya
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — short update and actionable items so Acme sees progress: 

- Training slots: confirmed. I booked two 75-minute sessions on June 12 (intro + architecture walk) and June 19 (hands-on workshop). Invites sent to Jana and the Acme pilot team.
- Enablement owners: Laura Bennett (me) will own the intro session; Diego will co-run the hands-on with me. Diego is out of this thread but is aware.
- Playbook items to publish by 6/5 EOD: quickstart (steps to integrate SDK + sample prompts), prompt_library_v1.md (with rubrics), and the training workbook (training_schedule_v1.xlsx). I uploaded a draft to the Drive link Marcus shared and added a short checklist in the doc for runbook steps.
- Reviewer pool: I can coordinate 4 reviewers from CS and DX for the manual spot checks on 6/5; please confirm time window and expected deliverable format (spreadsheet with pass/fail + notes).

Action items / owners: 
- Aditya: reserve Dedicated slot tonight 11pm-2am PT (or tell us if not possible) and run warmup before the smoke test.
- Marissa: finalize the 50 canonical prompts and add pass/fail rubrics to prompt_library_v1.md.
- Marcus: confirm whether we want to run the smoke validation against production traffic or a mirrored test stream. My preference is mirrored test stream unless we have explicit customer signoff.

Jana — appreciate if you can share 10 domain prompts by EOD 6/4 so we can prioritize. If procurement needs a formal schedule or SOW, I looped procurement in.

Laura Bennett
Enablement Lead, Redwood Inference
